about: Candidate Boolean model of ERK-dependent negative feedback in the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cascade, applied to MEK inhibition in colorectal cancer cell lines as reported by Fritsche-Guenther et al. 2011 (doi 10.1038/msb.2011.27). Fixed before the results sections of that paper were read. A retrospective reproduction and applicability assessment of published observations, not a holdout, blinded or independent test: the paper's title and section titles were seen before the model was fixed (see PREREG.md, category C).

models.description: Base model. ERK-dependent negative feedback acts on RAF; a BRAF V600E-type RAF is insensitive to it; KRAS-mutant RAS is active regardless of input.

components.description: growth-factor input from 10% fetal calf serum in culture
activating KRAS mutation present (genotype, assumed from the cell line)
BRAF V600E present (genotype, assumed from the cell line)
RAF kinase activity toward MEK (Raf-1 and B-Raf not separated)
MEK1 phosphorylated at its activating sites
Raf-1 phosphorylated at S289/S296/S301 (a readout node only; no rule reads it)

assumptions: 10% fetal calf serum is a continuous growth-factor input that activates wild-type RAS (the cited span states the culture medium only).
An activating KRAS mutation keeps RAS active regardless of input (general knowledge, not read in any source here).
RAS receives no ERK-dependent feedback in this model; this is the key unknown that M2 changes.

The source reports RAF signaling as feedback down-regulated in RTK-driven tumour cells; stating active ERK as a complete veto on RAS-driven RAF activity (NOT pERK) is a host strengthening, not what the source says.
The source reports BRAF-mutant RAF signaling as insensitive to that feedback; stating BRAF V600E as sufficient for RAF activity on its own (OR) is a host strengthening.
The source is a different system (RTK-driven and BRAF-mutant tumour lines); its applicability to KRAS-mutant colorectal lines is assumed.
RAS active is treated as sufficient for RAF activity when ERK is inactive; RAS binding RAF is not shown to activate it in any span read here.
MEK1 activating-site phosphorylation needs RAF activity and nothing else in this model.
The MEK inhibitor does not prevent RAF from phosphorylating MEK; it blocks only MEK's own kinase activity (intervention-mapping assumption, not read in any source here).
Phosphorylated MEK is sufficient for ERK phosphorylation unless a MEK inhibitor is present.
The MEK inhibitor, at the doses used, blocks MEK kinase activity completely (a Boolean veto); partial inhibition is not represented.

Phosphorylation of Raf-1 at S289/S296/S301 depends on active ERK (general knowledge; the cited span only names it feedback phosphorylation of Raf-1 and says the MEK inhibitor has an effect on it, without a direction).
Phosphorylation at these sites is a readout here, not the mechanism of the feedback; the feedback rule (M1_R_RAF or M2_R_RAS) reads pERK, not pRaf1fb.

models.description: Alternative for one key unknown rule: where the ERK-dependent feedback acts. Here it acts on wild-type RAS activation by the growth-factor input, and RAF follows RAS (or BRAF V600E) without feedback of its own. Every other rule is as in M1. A sensitivity check, fixed with M1 and not tuned afterwards.

window.why: Fixed before computing. Late enough for any transient of a five-node model to have passed, and seven steps long, so it covers a whole period of any cycle up to period 7 (a three-node negative loop under synchronous update has periods 1, 2 or 6). Steps are logical updates, not time.

initial_why: No internal state at the start is known; all five are left unknown and every one of the 32 combinations is run. Scenario and baseline share the initial state, so each case is paired.

KRAS.basis: KRAS-mutant status is general knowledge, not read in any source here (assumption).

BRAF.basis: BRAF V600E status is general knowledge, not read in any source here (assumption).

no_scenario.basis: No scenario was fixed for these systems; observations in them are not comparable.

assumptions: The bead signal reads activating-site MEK1 phosphorylation; a change in the cell population's signal is read as the direction of the model state.

readouts.basis: Immunoblot with anti-phospho-p44/42 MAPK Thr202/Tyr204, lit-e9c4f50cc489.
assumptions: The immunoblot reads ERK1/2 phosphorylation at T202/Y204; a change in the population's signal is read as the direction of the model state.
The immunoblot reads Raf-1 phosphorylation at these sites; a change in the population's signal is read as the direction of the model state.

readouts.basis: Active Ras pulldown with GST-Raf-1-RBD after 2 h AZD6244, lit-6100b8bafe2d.
assumptions: The pulldown reads GTP-bound RAS of all isoforms; a change in the population's signal is read as the direction of the model state.

questions.intervention: MEK inhibitor with cycloheximide or actinomycin D vs MEK inhibitor alone
questions.why: The models have no translation or transcription node; neither drug can be mapped to an input or clamp.

strict.rule: For the question's comparison, take the engine's per-case paired direction (readouts[].paired) for the readout at every step of the window. If every case at every window step gives the same direction (increase, decrease or no_change), that is the model's direction. Anything else (mixed directions, undetermined, a not-computed value) is undetermined.

ordinal.rule: Host aggregation, declared here before computing. Per case and per side, classify the readout's state over the window: always_active (true at every window step), always_inactive (false at every window step), intermittent (both values occur). A window containing a not-computed value is undetermined. Order always_inactive < intermittent < always_active; the case's direction is increase, decrease or no_change by that order. If every case gives the same direction, that is the model's direction; otherwise undetermined.
ordinal.assumption: An intermittent model state is read as an intermediate population level. That cells in a population are out of phase, or that the population signal averages over them, is not shown.

classification.부합: The text read states a direction (increase, decrease or no change versus untreated) for the question's readout in a cell line of the question's group, and the model's direction under the reading is the same.
classification.불일치: Both directions are determinate and differ.
classification.미결정: The text states a direction, but the model's direction under the reading is undetermined.
classification.비교 불가: No direction for the question is stated in the text read (a figure, table or supplement not read counts as not read); or the cell system has no scenario; or the intervention or the readout has no mapping (O6).
rules: Each observation statement found is one row. Several statements for one question are several rows; none is merged or dropped.
A statement about magnitude (e.g. how strongly, how efficiently, at which dose) is compared for direction only; its magnitude part is recorded as not comparable, because the model is Boolean.
Time points in the text (minutes, hours) are recorded beside the row. They are not converted to steps and do not change the class; a mismatch of timing is listed as a limit.
A statement found in the results that answers no question here is listed as unregistered and not scored.
Every row stays in every denominator, including 미결정 and 비교 불가.
